messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: Active ingredient: semaglutide Inactive ingredients:
Ozempic injection: disodium phosphate dihydrate, propylene glycol, phenol, and water for injections.
Ozempic has a pH of approximately 7.4.
Hydrochloric acid or sodium hydroxide may be added to adjust pH.
Ozempic tablet: magnesium stearate and salcaprozate sodium
Wegovy injection: disodium phosphate dihydrate, sodium chloride, and water for injection.
Phenol and propylene glycol are also inactive ingredients in the single-patient-use Wegovy FlexTouch.
Hydrochloric acid or sodium hydroxide may be added to adjust pH.
Wegovy tablets: salcaprozate sodium (SNAC) and magnesium stearate
Rybelsus R1 formulation: magnesium stearate, microcrystalline cellulose, povidone, and salcaprozate sodium (SNAC).
Rybelsus R2 formulation: magnesium stearate and salcaprozate sodium (SNAC).
Triplet: ["semaglutide", "may have added", "hydrochloric acid"]

The relation 'may have added' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may have the substance specified by the object entity added to it.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'may be used for': The subject drug may be used for the purpose or condition specified by the object entity.
B. 'has effect': The subject drug produces the effect specified by the object entity.
C. 'has note': The subject drug has an additional note or clarification provided that is specified by the object entity.
D. 'may be prescribed with': The subject drug may be prescribed in combination with the medication specified by the object entity.
E. 'similar to': The subject drug is related to or an alternative for the drug specified by the object entity.
F. None of the above.

Answer:
